articles.title: School Food
articles.author: Charlotte Jones
articles.excerpt: School food it's not always the topic of discussion, but it's very important to learn about what schools are feeding our students. In this article it will discuss how school food is now. How it is outside and inside TLC, how nutritious it is, and how the students of TLC can benefit from it.
articles.body:
What is wrong with American school food nowadays? It seems as though every video you scroll through about school food is another bad apple being served to students. But is our school food healthy? In this article we will talk about American school food and how our school food compares.

    How is American school food now?

    Public schools are probably the most affected by the non-nutritious foods. Sadly most schools aren’t paid enough from the government, so the food nutrition decreases. Their food is described as being unhealthy, and students would rather skip lunch than eat their school lunch. School lunch should be reliable and consumable, and from videos people show their school food is far from it, sadly mainly due to the schools budget. The good side of school food is, it’s a sustenance kids can eat when they're hungry. It's good to have something in your stomach for breakfast, lunch, and dinner.  

    Is TLC’s food any better?

    TLC food is a nutritious lunch for kids to eat. It not only has Lunch provided, but students can also get breakfast from 8:05 to 9:45. Our school shows what school lunch will be.

    When you're outside you’ll see what’s on the menu. A huge whiteboard shows what type of food we can receive, before having to wait in a long line. Not only that but TLC offers a “Share Table” where if there's food on your tray you may not want, that's unopened and untouched. You can put it in a box, so students don't waste it, and others have a little extra snack. Something that stands out is that TLC has different options, multiple choices. Like non-meat options for vegetarians and soy milk for the lactose intolerant. Our school is inclusive and shows it values their students' overall health. 

    When going inside the lunch room, just walking in students see nutrition posters. It also describes the food they’re serving. The food is separated, and students are required to at least grab one fruit or vegetable. And are welcome to put it in the share box if the students don’t feel like eating an item. After you pick your lunch, there's also a fridge that also stores food. It makes sure food  stays cold during the California heat.

    So students of TLC should be glad to have this wide variety of food options, flexible times to get food, and nutritious meals that are FREE. So next time you get yourself a tray of breakfast or lunch, make sure to thank them for that beneficial meal.



Works Cited

articles.title: Artificial Intelligence, is it bad to use?
articles.author: Charlotte Jones
articles.excerpt: Does AI deserve a chance? What good and bad can come from using it? And how could we be using it wisely? In this article we will discuss the basics of using AI.
articles.body:
Can Artificial Intelligence be useful?
AI is often seen as being a horrible invention, but what AI helps us with is sometimes overlooked. It can be used to explain things, easily give information from sources, and generate things in a very small amount of time that sometimes would be difficult to picture. Not everyone is creative, and it makes people's lives easier using it. Like in healthcare, it spots early signs of cancer, heart trouble, and fractures faster than humans can. On the other hand, AI can also be dangerous. This article will cover the good and bad of AI.

Why can Artificial Intelligence be bad?
Artificial intelligence can also be harmful. With an imperfect human trying to make a perfect Intelligence, there is a chance of it becoming biased. Since we all have our own thinking, it might be hard to make a completely unbiased AI. For example, someone creates an AI that’s supposed to give helpful information about how you should use your time. It is a great way to find tips and useful advice. This can seem helpful on the surface, but AI can become biased easily because it’s based on the creator’s beliefs. Would if the creator believed that people should spend most of their time making money? Then the AI will be more likely to show people how they can spend their time in the workplace. Which isn’t good because we want Artificial Intelligence to be perfectly unbiased. Not only that, but having artificial intelligence doing everything for you can cause a decrease in human intelligence, and it reduces the use of critical thinking. And it is very important that everyone continues to exorcise their brains day-to-day. Lastly, something most people like to bring up when arguing about how Artificial Intelligence can be bad, is how it uses our water. Let's delve deeper into the question: is Artificial Intelligence really taking our water?

Does Artificial Intelligence use our water?
When talking about Artificial Intelligence, someone’s main argument is that it uses our water. Accoording to the CBS article, “Google says a typical AI query uses five drops of water.” That may not seem like much, but  it can easily add up. It’s like when you accidentally leave your sink water on, one drop per second. It barely seems like anything, but when left unattended for only one day it can drip 86,400 times. Which is 5.7 gallons of water wasted in one day.  But the article also states: “The answer can depend on the AI model, the data center's location and the mix of sources in the local power grid. The amount can differ by hundreds of times over.” So the water usage all depends on the type of AI model you're using and how much you’re using it. 

Should we be using Artificial Intelligence?
Using Artificial intelligence is, like most things, a conscious decision. In this article we have talked about the good and bad parts of Artificial Intelligence. So now, it’s up to the readers. Do you think it's okay to use artificial intelligence? What precautions will you take to save the earth's water, and how can you use artificial intelligence intelligently and wisely?
